[{"id": "nnvMTG5Sl5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83c\udf10Website Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "B-CtTCmVDX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The website module consists of two main features: a public website, and a user portal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fAFxFk8rny", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "\ud83c\udf0eWebsite", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WCW6FzkHwB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The public facing website is accessible by anyone and can be dynamically updated based on information in the Church App (i.e. Beliefs, Missionaries, Ministries, etc).
The Web Site workspace shows the number of web pages and a chart of web pages by type. Below them it shows the home page as a visitor sees it. Click the preview to open the website in a new tab. The sidebar lists Web Pages, Web Forms, Website Settings, Website Themes, About Us Settings and Contact Us Settings. Portal Settings, Website Script, Website Sidebars and Website Route Meta are in Setup.
User accounts with \"Church Manager\" permissions can modify the website by editing the website settings and publishing documents.
The website menu is the Top Bar Items table in Website Settings, and pages themselves are Web Page records. Publishing a Web Page adds it to the end of the menu. Un-publishing or deleting one removes its links from the menu and footer. A message confirms each change. Rename or move the new item in the Top Bar Items table. Editing a page that is already published does not put it back on the menu. Removing a link from the menu does not take its page down: after you save, the app offers to un-publish any Web Page that link pointed at. Answer No to keep the page reachable by its address.
The shipped pages (Home, Beliefs, Sermons, Missions, Ministries) are yours to edit; an upgrade leaves your wording alone and only ever repairs the record-reading code inside a page. Open one under Web Page: the content is in Main Section (HTML), a Jinja template (Content Type HTML with Dynamic Template on) that reads your published records, so the page updates itself as you publish sermons, beliefs, missionaries and so on. Prefer to write a page by hand? Switch Content Type to Rich Text or Markdown. Per-page styles go in the Custom CSS tab; the site-wide look is the Website Theme. To restore a shipped page's original look, copy its template from the app source (churchit/patches/after_install/templates/) back into Main Section (HTML).
No user account is required to view the website - anyone with an internet connection and a web browser can view the public website.
The site's look is a Website Theme, chosen under Website Settings \u2192 Website Theme: Churchit (the shipped look) or Frappe's plain Standard. Each has a light and a dark mode; visitors switch with the sun/moon button in the navbar, and the site follows their device setting until they do. On a phone, a tablet or a small laptop (a screen narrower than 1200 pixels), the menu button opens the site links and a Dark mode or Light mode switch. That list leaves out Home, because the church name at the top left opens the home page.
Every page ends with the same short footer: the church's name and founding year from the Church record on the left; the phone number from Contact Us Settings and the church address on the right (the address opens in OpenStreetMap); the copyright from Website Settings \u2192 Footer, if set, in the middle; and the footer links from the same tab centred underneath. The Contact Us page shows that same church address unless Contact address differs from the church address is checked in Contact Us Settings, which reveals fields for a different one. When there is no address, the column on the Contact Us page has the title Contact and shows only the phone number and email address.
Any field shown outside the desk is marked beside its label: an outgoing-link badge when anyone can see it, a people badge when only signed-in members can. Hover the badge to see which pages or portal forms show that field, and click it to open one. On a phone, tap the badge to see that list, then tap Open page. The marks are read from the pages themselves, so a page, portal form or public link added later is marked without anyone listing it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LXwizYK5zu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "About Us page. The About Us page shows the About text of the Church record. It shows the introduction in About Us Settings only when the Church record has no About text. Write your main introduction in the About tab of the Church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "GAJDYQfXXs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Keyboard. On every page, the first press of Tab shows the link Skip to content. Press Enter on it to go past the menu to the content of the page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r11MenuHead", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\udded Add an Item to the Website Menu", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r11MenuText", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Some pages are not in the website menu by default, for example the Announcements page (/announcements) and the Watch Live page (/live). A Church Manager, or any user with the Website Manager role, can add them:
1. Open Website Settings and click the Navbar tab.
2. In the Top Bar Items table, click Add Row.
3. In Label, type the name to show in the menu, for example Announcements or Watch Live.
4. In URL, type the address of the page, for example /announcements or /live.
5. Click the edit icon at the end of the new row and tick Align Right. The menu items that Churchit installs have this box ticked, so the new item then shows next to them. When you publish a page, Churchit adds its item without this box ticked, and that item shows on the left. Tick Align Right on that item too to show it with the others.
6. To move the item, drag its row up or down.
7. Save.
When a page is off in Church Features, the menu does not show its item. With more than one church, the item opens the page of the church that the visitor selected.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YdfkxozE4J", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Logo in the menu bar. To show your logo in the website menu bar, open Website Settings, click the Navbar tab and set Brand Image. The menu bar then shows the logo in place of the church name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "TJOwFE61be", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Footer links. The footer at the bottom of each page has three links: I'm New opens the Connection Card, Prayer Request opens the prayer request form for visitors, and Member Portal opens the member portal. To change these links, open Website Settings, click the Footer tab and change the Footer Items table. When a page is off in Church Features, the footer does not show its link. If you remove all the footer links on purpose, an update does not put them back. The login page also shows the footer, with the name of your church and its links. To hide it, open Website Settings and clear Show Footer on Login.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "calFeedHeader1", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcc5 Calendar Feed", "col": 12, "level": 4}}, {"id": "calFeedText01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Calendar page has two buttons above the calendar. Subscribe adds the calendar to the calendar app of a phone or computer. Download .ics saves the calendar as a file. Both give the calendar of the church that the page shows, without its branch churches. The link is https://<your site>/api/method/churchit.ics.get_public_calendar.
- The feed shows the same functions as the Calendar page: published functions from one month ago to six months ahead, with their address, description and online meeting link. Functions with Link Only ticked are not in the feed.
- With more than one church, add ?church=<church ID> to show the calendar of one published church.
- Add ministry=<ministry> to show only the functions of one published ministry, for example ?church=CHR-01&ministry=Youth. A ministry that is not published gives an empty calendar.
Calendar apps check the link for changes by themselves.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "vB5Ph8mulz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On a phone. The Calendar page opens as a list of the events of the month. Tap month to see the grid. An event that lasts more than one day shows on each of its days, and its details show the first and the last day.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "daCjIXQkxY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Event details. Click an event to open its details in a window. Press Tab to move inside the window, and press Escape to close it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "locWebHeader1", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udccd Locations (Multi-Church)", "col": 12, "level": 4}}, {"id": "locWebIntro01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Switch on Enable Multi-Church in the Multi-Church section of Church Features and the website can show all of your churches, not just the main one. Open each Church and tick Publish to put it on the website. That is the only step. A church you leave unpublished does not appear anywhere on the site.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "locWebSwitch1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Once two or more churches are published, a Locations item appears in the website menu, beside Home. On a screen narrower than 1280 pixels, a signed-in member's menu leaves out Home so that all the links stay on one row (the church name at the top left opens the home page). The church that the page shows has (selected) after its name. On a screen narrower than 1200 pixels, Locations is in the list that the menu button opens. It lists every published church, and All locations at the bottom opens the Locations page, which shows a card for each church with its photo, mission statement, description and address. The photo is the Image of the Church. Visitors see it only when it is a public file. The Study manual tells how to make it public.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "locWebFollow1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When a visitor picks a location, the whole website switches to that church and stays there as they move from page to page. These follow the choice:
- the church name in the website menu, and the address and phone number in the footer
- the home page, calendar, sermons, ministries, missions and bulletins
- the funds offered on the Give page
- the About Us page, which shows that church's own About and Mission Statement when it has them, and the main church's wording when it does not
- anything a visitor sends in from those pages, such as a prayer request, which belongs to the church whose page they used", "col": 12}}, {"id": "locWebNotes01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A few things worth knowing:
- A record ticked Shared with all churches, such as a sermon, a song or a room, appears on every church's pages. The Foundations manual explains sharing.
- A member who is signed in sees their own church first, whether or not it is published. The member portal always shows the member's own church.
- The Contact page sends each message to the church whose page the visitor is on. A message from a branch's page goes to the email of that branch. A message from the main church's page, or from a branch with no email, goes to Forward To Email in Contact Us Settings, or to the main church's email when that is empty. Each message is also kept on the church: open the Church and look at its activity at the bottom of the form. When Send Acknowledgement Email is ticked in Contact Us Settings, the visitor gets a short thank-you email with the name of the church.
- If only one church is published, or multi-church is switched off, there is no Locations item and the website looks exactly as it does for a single church.
- While multi-church is off, the Locations page does not exist, and no menu, footer or site map link goes to it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10LiveHead", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcfa Watch Live", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10LiveText", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To show your live stream on the website, open the Church and, in the Contact section of the Details tab, put the link to the stream in Live Stream Link. The link must start with https://. The /live page then shows the stream:
1. A YouTube video link, a youtube.com/channel/ link that ends in /live, a Let's Church media link, a PeerTube video link or an Owncast player link (it ends in /embed/video) plays on the page.
2. Any other link, such as a youtube.com/@name/live link, opens the site of the stream.
3. A branch church without its own link uses the link of its parent church.
4. If no church above the selected one has a link, /live shows \"Page not found\".
The Calendar page shows a Watch live button on each function with Streamed ticked while it runs. The Ministries manual tells more. The website menu has no Watch Live item by itself. To add one, see Add an Item to the Website Menu above, and use the URL /live.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r11LiveYouTube", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A YouTube channel. A youtube.com/@name/live link does not play on the page. It opens YouTube. To play the stream of your channel on the page, use the link with your channel ID: https://www.youtube.com/channel/channel ID/live. A channel ID starts with UC, for example UCabcdefghijklmnopqrstuv. To find it, sign in to YouTube with the channel account and open https://www.youtube.com/account_advanced. Copy the Channel ID. You can also open your channel page, click more about this channel, click Share channel and click Copy channel ID. This link always plays the stream that is live now, so you do not change it for each service.
A channel link does not play in every browser. After you set the link, open /live and make sure that the stream plays. If it does not play, use the watch link of the stream, for example https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=video ID. A watch link plays one stream only, so put the new link on the Church before each service.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10MembersHead", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udd12 Members-only Pages", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10MembersText", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To show a web page only to members, open the Web Page, tick Members Only and save. A visitor who is not signed in goes to the login page and comes back to the page after login. A signed-in user who is not an active member, for example a visitor or a contact, sees a Not Permitted message. Staff who can edit web pages can always open the page. A members-only page does not show in the website search.
A link to a members-only page in the menu, the footer or the portal shows only to the people who can open the page. Other visitors do not see the link or the page title, and the page is not in the site map. This applies to links that use the page route as you see it on the page form. If you type the route in a different way, for example with an accent, the link shows to everyone, but the page stays closed.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "a4WebAiHead", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\ude84 Page Text with AI", "col": 12}}, {"id": "a4WebAiText", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When AI is turned on (see the Foundations manual), a Web Page has two AI links. They show only for a saved page that is published and is not Members Only, because only then can everyone read its text. Nothing is saved: you save the page yourself.
- Description in the Meta Tags section has Draft with AI. It writes the short text that search engines show (see Draft with AI in the Communications manual).
- Main Section has Alt Text with AI, when Content Type is Rich Text. Alt text is the text that a screen reader says for a picture. The AI cannot see the pictures. It reads the text of the page and the file name of each picture, and it writes one short alt text of at most 125 characters for each picture that has none. A picture that has alt text keeps it. When the page and the file name do not tell what a picture shows, the AI writes \"Photo from the church\". Click Use to put the alt texts in the pictures, then check each one and save the page.
A page that is not saved, not published or for members only gets neither link, and a page with the Content Type HTML gets no alt text link. The AI gets only the text that guests can read, so any model can answer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "a7WebTransHead", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "\ud83c\udf0d Translate with AI", "col": 12}}, {"id": "a7WebTransText1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When AI is turned on (see the Foundations manual), a saved Web Page that is published and not Members Only has the button Translate with AI. You must be able to write Web Pages. The page needs Rich Text, Markdown or HTML content of at most 12000 characters.
1. Click Translate with AI and choose a language. The list holds the languages that are enabled on the site.
2. The AI gets only the title, the content and the meta description of the page. They are published text. Nothing else goes.
3. Click Open Draft. A new Web Page opens, not saved and not published. Its title is the translated title with the language name in brackets. Its route is the route of the page, a dash and the language code, for example about-es. It keeps the layout and style settings of the page, but not its JavaScript and context script. Copy them yourself when the page needs them.
Churchit refuses the answer, and opens no draft, when the AI changed a template tag ({{ }} or {% %}) or added a script, a style, a frame, an event handler or a link to another site.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "a7WebTransText2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A fluent person must check it. AI makes mistakes in every language, and more in a rare language. It can change the meaning of a belief or a name, or use a word that sounds wrong to a native speaker. Before you publish the draft, ask a person who speaks the language well, and who knows what your church believes, to read it. After the first save, the timeline says that AI helped. Any Privacy Label is allowed, because the text of the page is already public.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10PagesHead", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udd0c Turn a Website Page Off", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10PagesText1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open Church Features and open the Website Pages section. It opens by itself while a page is off. Each page that Churchit puts on the website has one row. Clear Enabled on a row and save to take that page off the website. Visitors then get \"Page not found\", the form on that page takes no new entries, and the links to the page go from the menu, the footer, the member portal and the site map. Nothing is deleted, and the records in the desk do not change. Tick Enabled again to bring the page and its links back.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10PagesText2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When you clear a module in Church Features, its website pages go too. For example, with Study off, the Sermons, sermon, podcast, Bible and Bible Memory pages are off. Web Site is different: it hides only the desk tools, and the public website stays on. A page that you made yourself is not in this list. To take one of your own Web Pages off the website, clear its Published box. With the Sermons page off, the home page does not show the latest sermon, the link to all sermons or the sermon count. With the Calendar or Contact page off, the home page does not show its buttons and links to that page. If you changed your home page, check it for links to pages that are off.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r306NoSiteText", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "No public website. If your church already has its own website, open Church Features, tick Turn Off the Public Website in the Website Pages section and save. A visitor who is not signed in then gets only the login page, also at the address of the site, and the menu, the footer and the site map show them no page links. Members sign in and keep the member portal and the other pages that are on, such as Calendar, Give and Bulletins. Visitors cannot give online or sign up for a function until they sign in. The pages about the church go for members too: Home, Beliefs, Sermons, Missions, Ministries, About Us, Contact Us, Locations, Watch Live, Find a Group, the Connection Card, the prayer request form for visitors, and each of your own Web Pages that is not Members Only. The podcast feed stays on, and the link in a ministry team request email still opens for someone who has no login. Clear the box and save to bring the website back.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lookHead", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "\ud83c\udfa8 Colors and Look", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lookIntro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The website and the member portal share one look, set like a printed bulletin: serif titles, a double line under each page title and fine lines between entries. The colors come from the Website Theme. To pick one, open Website Settings and, in the Theme section, click a theme in the picker under Website Theme, then save. Each card shows the light and the dark page of its theme. Click Preview on a card to open your home page in that theme before you save. Only you see the preview.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lookThemes", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit ships six themes: Churchit (warm paper with a deep red, the default), Harbor (navy), Meadow (green), Indigo, Vesper (plum) and Slate (gray with a teal). Standard is the plain white and gray of Frappe. The member portal takes the same colors, so members see one church in both places.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lookOwn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Your own colors. Open a theme in Website Theme, click Duplicate in its menu, give the copy a name and change three colors: Background Color is the paper, Text Color the ink and Primary Color the accent, which marks today's date and a few other things. The page stays light with dark text, and the accent stays easy to read in light and dark mode, whatever colors you pick. Then pick your theme in Website Settings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lookLive", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Live updates. An open page updates by itself a few seconds after staff publish or change something that it shows: an event on the home page, the Calendar and the Register page, a sermon on the home page and the Sermons page, announcements, and the number of ministries and missionaries on the home page. The new rows show with a short highlight. A visitor does not need to reload the page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "appHead", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcf1 The App on Phones and Computers", "col": 12}}, {"id": "appIntro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members and staff can install the website as an app on a phone or computer. The app has the name and icon of your church and opens in its own window. Under the icon, a phone shows the church name when it has 12 characters or fewer, or else the Abbreviation of the Church. Staff open on the desk and members open on the member portal. On a phone, touch and hold the icon to go straight to the Calendar, Prayer Request, Give or Sermons page. On a computer, right-click it. A page that is off is not in that list.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "appOffer", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The install offer: After a user signs in, a card at the bottom of the page offers the app. On Android, and in Chrome or Edge on a computer, Install opens the install dialog of the browser. Edge then lets the user pin the app to the taskbar or the Start menu. In Chrome, right-click the open app in the taskbar and click Pin to taskbar. On an iPhone or iPad, the card tells the user to tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. In Safari on a Mac, it tells them to choose File, then Add to Dock. Firefox and Zen on a computer cannot install apps, so they show no card. The card does not show in the installed app, on the Check In page or in a sermon presentation.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "appLater", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Not now: Not now hides the card on that device for 30 days. Then it shows again. A user can install the app at any time: staff click Install App in the user menu, and members click Install under Install the app on the Preferences page of the member portal. Both show only while the browser can install the app. On an iPhone or iPad, Safari cannot tell if the app is already on the Home Screen, so the card can come back in Safari after 30 days.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "appSwitch", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Turn the offer off: Open Church Features, clear Offer to Install the App in the App section and save. The card then does not show by itself. Install App, the Communication Preferences button and the install item in the browser menu stay.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10BuilderHead", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\uddf1 Pages made with Frappe Builder", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10BuilderText", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Frappe Builder is a separate app to design web pages by drag and drop. A System Manager can install it next to Churchit and make new pages with it. Note the following:
1. A Builder page takes its address before Churchit pages, web forms and Web Pages. Before you use an address, open it in a private window. Use it only when it shows \"Page not found\".
2. Do not use an address that is listed under Website Pages in Church Features, also when that page is off. A page that is off shows \"Page not found\" in place of a Builder page at that address.
3. A Builder page cannot keep the records of one church apart from the others. Show church records, such as events, sermons or people, only on Churchit pages, and link to those pages from your Builder page.
4. Churchit does not put its website badge on the fields that a Builder page shows.
5. The shipped pages (Home, Beliefs, Missions, Ministries and Sermons) stay Web Pages. Churchit ships no Builder pages.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nZdduTPzRH", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udc64User Portal", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8qBfIl0adi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The member portal is an app at /portal that members and staff open with their login, on a phone or a computer. In the desk, staff who have a Person record open the menu at the top of the sidebar and choose Member Portal. It shows only what belongs to the person or what is shared with them, such as the prayer requests the church shares. A visitor who is not signed in goes to the login page, which tells them to ask the church office for a login and offers the Connection Card (when Show Footer on Login is ticked in Website Settings). The old addresses of the portal pages, such as /household or /function-sign-up/new, open the same page in the app, so the links in emails and bookmarks keep working.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pSbMnu7rQe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The menu. On a computer the menu is a column on the left. On a phone, five tabs sit at the bottom: This week, Check-in (or Sign-Ups when your church does not use self check-in), Groups, Prayer, and More, which opens everything else. The menu is the Menu table in Portal Settings (open Setup in the Web Site sidebar). The Role on each row controls who sees it. To add, remove or rename a page in the menu, change that table. A row for a page outside the app, such as one you add yourself, opens that page. The app adds This week, Check-in, Give and the links to the church website. A page that is turned off in Church Features leaves the menu, and its address answers \"Page not found\".", "col": 12}}, {"id": "app-week", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This week. The first page shows the member's week: what they signed up for, when they serve and when their groups meet. When check-in is open, the first thing on the page is a button to check in. A request to serve sits in a box with the buttons Yes, I can and I can't this time. Beside the week are the bulletin's notices, the newest prayer requests with an I prayed button, the latest bulletin, and the members-only pages the member can open (see Members-only Pages above). The prayer requests and the notices each open their own page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "app-household", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Household and check-in. My Household shows the people in the household, the household photo and the address. An adult of the household can change the photo, add a child, and edit their own details and the details of their children. To add another adult or to remove someone, the member asks the church office. When your church uses self check-in, the member opens Check-in a little before the service, chooses who is coming and taps Show our pass. Name tags print when a volunteer scans the pass at the door, and the page shows each person as they are checked in. When everyone is in, the page says so. If a member has trouble at the door, a volunteer can check them in by name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "app-details", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "My details and preferences. My Details lets a member change their name, birthday, allergies, email addresses, phone numbers and marital status, and choose what other members see about them in the directory. The church office changes the address. If someone changed the record while the member had it open, the page asks them to reload it and make the change again. Preferences lets a member choose, for each kind of message, how they get it, turn notifications on or off for the device they use, install the app on the home screen, and switch between light and dark mode.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "app-signups", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Sign-ups and attendance. The Sign-Ups page has three tabs. Upcoming lists the member's places at functions with their status: Confirmed, Pending (the church must approve it), Waitlisted (the function is full) or Cancelled. Open lists the functions that take sign-ups now. Attended is the attendance history. A member signs up for a simple function in the app. A function with questions or choices opens the church's sign-up page, /register, instead. While sign-ups are open, a member can change or cancel their sign-up; a place that a cancel frees goes to the next person on the waitlist. When the church allows it, a member can correct a past row to say whether they were there.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "app-serving", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Serving and rooms. Serving shows where the member is asked to serve. A request that waits for an answer sits at the top. A member can ask someone else on the team to take their place, add the dates they cannot serve, and set how many times a month they serve in each position. Room Requests lists the rooms the member asked for and the answer to each: Requested, Approved, Denied or Conflict. A member can change a request that is still to come unless the office denied it. On a room that needs approval, an approved request goes back to Requested when the member moves its room or time. A booking that the church office made for the member is not listed.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "app-groups", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Groups. Groups shows the groups the member is in, when they meet and who leads them, and the public groups of their church to join or ask to join. A member who opens one of their groups sees who else is in it: each person's name, their photo if it is public, and who leads the group.
